{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Contracts

Blue Contracts processes an event against exact managed Blue documents and returns
the resulting state, ordered emitted occurrences, deterministic gas and replay
evidence. It uses Language for content semantics and BEX for evaluation.

## Final gas edition

`1.0.0-final-gas.1` retains the existing tariffs and the 10,000,000-gas shared
maximum. Each charge is checked before work happens. Canonical outcomes contain
the final admitted gas total and, on exhaustion, one rejected-charge diagnostic.
They do not contain per-charge histories. Turn and unit proofs carry scalar gas
contributions, and continuation commitments carry totals and configured local
counters. Removing the history does not remove budget enforcement or replay
verification.

`SPECIFICATION.md` and `spec/contracts-final-gas.md` are the same normative text,
including eighteen executable Python modules. Source overrides and their hashes
are listed in `docs/sources.json`; the earlier reference remains frozen.
The 32 native type definitions are generated by the specification's catalogue
recipe. `types/` contains authoring inputs and `docs/types/` their exact views.

The specification, types, packages and receipts have new exact identities. A host
must explicitly install this edition. Keep the original runtime when replaying
old snapshots or histories; see [migration](MIGRATION.md).

## Local verification

With Python 3.13+, pytest, PyYAML, Java 21 and `BLUE_JAVA_CLASSPATH` pointing to
the qualified Java Language runtime and its dependencies:

```sh
./blue-package verify
./blue-package demo
./blue-package test
python ../tools/build_final_gas.py blue-contracts --check
```

The rebuild check compares the full archive, unpacked distribution and dependency
lock without modifying the selected publication. Package verification alone does
not certify a host implementation. [Qualification](QUALIFICATION.md) distinguishes
the new edition from earlier reference reports.
"}

It evaluates against explicit inputs and produces a value, an ordered changeset, ordered events and a deterministic admitted gas total. BEX does not perform document mutation or select externally ordered inputs. ## Contents - [1. Scope and conformance](#scope) - [2. Exact dependencies and interpretation](#dependencies) - [3. Purpose and imported language](#section-3) - [4. Machine and invocation](#section-4) - [5. Value domains and absence](#section-5) - [6. Numeric and Text rules](#section-6) - [7. Source classification and static positions](#section-7) - [8. Evaluation order and laziness](#section-8) - [9. Reads and observations](#section-9) - [10. Pointers and ordered changesets](#section-10) - [11. Collections](#section-11) - [12. Variables, functions, and return](#section-12) - [13. Effects and host intrinsics](#section-13) - [14. Gas](#section-14) - [15. Blue output boundary](#section-15) - [16. Errors and determinism](#section-16) - [17. Executable inventory and conformance](#section-17) - [18. External capability boundary](#section-18) - [19. Composition with Language and Contracts](#section-19) - [20. Release and identity](#section-20) - [21. Immutable host values](#section-21) - [22. Shared host metering](#section-22) - [23. Resource-proportional work accounting](#section-23) - [24. Equality and conversion ordering](#section-24) - [25. Occurrence and effect traversal](#section-25) - [Appendix A. Complete operator reference](#operators) - [Appendix B. Complete executable algorithms](#algorithms) ## 1. Scope and conformance This specification defines the protocol identified by this edition. Its prose, tables and algorithm appendices form one normative contract. It is independent of source-repository branches, release tags, installation paths and prior discussions. Named external semantics are selected exactly in §2. Where an implementation uses another programming language, it MUST preserve the same specified observations; matching internal classes or diagnostic wording is not required unless explicitly identified as an observation. **MUST** and **REQUIRED** express requirements. **MUST NOT** and **PROHIBITED** express prohibitions. **SHOULD** and **SHOULD NOT** express recommendations whose departures require understood consequences. **MAY** and **OPTIONAL** express permissions. Examples marked informative do not add requirements. A conflict between normative prose and algorithms is a defect, not permission to choose an outcome. A finite conformance corpus is evidence, not a proof for every possible input. A package distributes this specification; it does not install a processor. The package's BlueId, this specification Text's BlueId and the OCI/archive digests identify different content. This document does not contain its own calculated identity or the generated identities of types that refer to it. ## 2. Exact dependencies and interpretation This edition selects Blue Language package `8XGYNufx24r7Dc5bGoeobcGNCn9roLzSfZCQyHBTaTx4`, whose complete specification Text is `H7WiYQ6GiWypRdFyWRcv99dsvTv6WnJYnu9eLYPQmWnc`. Node construction, exact references, specialization, output admission and BlueIds have the meaning defined by that Language release. BEX is independent of Contracts. A host may supply Language-backed matching, node identity, finite reads and explicit intrinsics. Contracts is one such host and binds the supplied BEX context and meter according to its own specification. BEX MUST NOT substitute ambient state or an unversioned implementation for these declared interfaces. Package imports supply exact content. Authoring prefixes are local bindings and do not leak through transitive imports. An imported definition retains its exact references. Mounting another package cannot change the selected interpreter or replace an existing type reference. Within this edition's interpreted package graph, the selected Language release MUST agree throughout; cross-Language conversion and mixed-rule cyclic sets are not defined. One selected Language governs a complete cyclic identity set and its owning proof. ## 3. Purpose and imported language BEX evaluates data-encoded programs against explicit, read-only inputs and produces values, ordered changesets, and ordered events. It neither fetches arbitrary resources nor publishes a document. A Contracts processor decides whether proposed effects can be applied; Coordination determines which authenticated external input is eligible. The reader is assumed to know Blue Language 1.0. Node admission, effective types, specialization, exact versus Source representations, references, set finalization, and BlueId are imported, not redefined. A BEX value is not a Blue node. In particular, Python object identity, dictionary iteration order, and native truth testing do not define BEX semantics. The executable algorithm appendix contains the complete evaluator and host-value algorithms. Readable rules and executable algorithms together define this edition; disagreement is a defect, not permission to choose either result. ## 4. Machine and invocation An invocation has a compiled program; an explicit context; a gas meter; lexical function frames; an ordered changeset; and an ordered event list. Context supplies the selected document snapshot, event, current contract, previous step results, named bindings, and executing scope. Optional adapters provide finite document reads, Blue specialization checks, and exact-type intrinsics. No process-global variable is a program binding. No Python expression is evaluated from program text. The interpreter recognizes data forms, not Python, JavaScript, or embedded shell commands. An installed intrinsic is trusted host code and is outside that sandbox boundary. A successful invocation returns `Result(value, changeset, events, gas_used)`. It does not apply its changes. Returned effects remain ordinary BEX values until the Contracts output boundary has validated and converted them. ## 5. Value domains and absence The domains are undefined, null, Text, Integer, Double, Boolean, Object, and List. `UNDEFINED` is a singleton distinct from Python `None`, which represents internal BEX null. Boolean is not Integer. Objects have Text keys. Integers use exact integer arithmetic; Doubles use finite decimal observations and cross the Blue Double boundary as finite binary64 values. Missing member lookup yields undefined. Undefined object members are omitted by Blue conversion. Undefined list elements, including sparse overlay holes, cannot cross that boundary. Null is not an empty object and is rejected at the Blue output boundary. An actual empty object remains an actual empty object. `$emptyObject` is the explicit empty-object constructor. `$exists` is false only for undefined. Null therefore exists. Truth is false for undefined, null, false, empty Text, empty Object, and empty List; other values are true, **including numeric zero**. `$empty` and `$isEmpty` test the inverse of this truth rule, not Python's truthiness. ## 6. Numeric and Text rules Integer conversion accepts integers, integral finite numbers, and canonical decimal integer text. Fractional values and noncanonical integer spellings fail. Numeric conversion rejects Boolean, collections, nonfinite numbers, and malformed numeric text. Arithmetic operators in this edition produce exact Integer results, and division requires an exact Integer quotient. Division by zero or a fractional quotient fails. Numeric equality compares numeric value across Integer and Double. Other equality is domain-sensitive and recursive. It must not be substituted for BlueId equality or Language specialization. Collections do not stringify implicitly. Null and undefined stringify to empty Text where coercion is allowed; names, paths, keys, and operation names require presence and cannot use that absence coercion. Text-key ordering is Unicode code-point ordering. Gas size estimation counts UTF-16 code units, not Python string length or UTF-8 bytes. These are different operations and must remain separate. Nonfinite Doubles and lone Unicode surrogates are invalid runtime values at the relevant boundary. There is no universal source-depth, call-frame, numeric-text, Integer-result-size or Blue-output Integer-length ceiling. Integer arithmetic, finite binary64 values, canonical text, static recursion rejection and output validity remain mandatory. A host that cannot compile or evaluate otherwise valid finite work reports operational incompleteness, not invalid syntax, a false arithmetic error or gas exhaustion. Gas is a logical work rule, not an operating-system resource sandbox. Large operand/allocation paths require correctly placed deterministic work charges and safe host isolation; a local machine failure cannot create a different semantic history. ## 7. Source classification and static positions A single-key object whose key starts with `$` is an executable form when encountered in expression or statement position. It must name an installed operator valid for that position. Other objects are recursively evaluated data constructors. `$literal` prevents evaluation of its payload as program data, but does not authorize executable material in static Blue definition positions. Type-related and schema positions are static. Constants and function-argument patterns are static. Compilation rejects unknown operators, invalid operand shapes, unknown variables/constants/functions, malformed static names, reserved user-container names, invalid call argument sets, and recursive function-call graphs. Both sides of a lazy runtime construct still undergo static validation. A function body selects `expr` ahead of `do`. An explicit named entry must exist and take no arguments. The implementation also validates the root body even when a named entry is selected. Definition constants/functions can be supplied as an already available object to the compiler; loading a referenced program definition is a host integration obligation. ## 8. Evaluation order and laziness Object constructors evaluate keys in deterministic order; lists evaluate left to right. Function arguments evaluate in key order. Lazy operators evaluate only the branch or subsequent operand needed to establish the result. This applies to Boolean connectives, coalescing/default selection, conditionals, and lookup defaults. A static error in an unused branch is still an error. A runtime error or gas charge in an unselected branch does not occur. Empty or missing values cannot be replaced by Python idioms such as `value or fallback` unless they implement the particular BEX operator's rule. ## 9. Reads and observations `$document`, `$event`, `$currentContract`, `$binding`, `$steps`, `$var`, and `$const` read only their designated source. A variable or constant name containing `/` remains a name; its optional pointer is a separate operand. A named step is addressed by the step's actual Language `name` label, not its list position when a name was supplied. A Compute invocation sees a stable selected-document snapshot. A later Compute step sees effects successfully applied by earlier steps. `$resultValue` overlays this invocation's accumulated changes on its snapshot; it does not publish them. Finite managed-document reads use the closure's selected dependency projection, never an independently advancing source's latest public head. The context's matcher implements `$is` using Blue semantic admission and specialization. The interpreter does not guess that a JSON shape is a valid Blue type. Missing patterns, unknown required definitions, and uninstalled matcher capabilities are not accepted as successful matches. ### Exact node identity `$nodeBlueId: EXPR` evaluates EXPR once and returns a Text containing the ordinary Language BlueId. Charge `nodeIdentityRequested = 5` after evaluating the operand and before calling the host's Language identity boundary. The boundary shares the invocation meter and cannot use a separate unmetered hash implementation. An admitted exact host collection retains its selected exact identity, including owning-set member identity, without expanding its descendants. A newly computed value passes the existing strict Blue-output validation and Language Exact admission/identity construction. Newly built containers preserve exact nested operands and their identity evidence; storage presentation cannot change charges. Null or undefined roots, malformed references, invalid type slots and incomplete owning-set evidence fail; missing required content is not replaced by an invented identity. Scalars are ordinary BEX scalar values and receive their corresponding Language scalar identity; metadata erased by scalar observation is not reconstructed. Equality and type specialization remain different operations from exact identity comparison. The standard Contracts context installs this boundary. Standalone BEX hosts supply `Context.node_blue_id(value, gas)` backed by the same Language operations; without it the operator fails with a boundary error. It does not perform network lookup or register user code. `processingEvent` remains a Contracts binding read through `$binding`; no `$processingEvent` operator is introduced. ## 10. Pointers and ordered changesets BEX value pointers use JSON-pointer escaping. Both empty Text and `/` designate the value root in this profile. This differs from the Language query API's empty-key behavior; adapters must not delegate blindly. Relative document paths resolve against the executing scope; already absolute document paths remain absolute. A Contracts processor separately checks whether a proposed absolute path is writable by that scope. A changeset is an ordered list of add, replace, or remove proposals. Non-remove proposals require a value. Remove ignores no hidden expression: its value operand is not evaluated by the append operation. Appending preserves duplicate operations and their order. BEX's observation overlay is **not** Contracts mutation. Overlay removal from a List creates a sparse undefined position and does not shift later elements. Actual Contracts array removal does shift later elements. Intermediate overlay objects are constructed deterministically. A sparse result may be observed internally but cannot be serialized as a Blue List containing undefined. ## 11. Collections Collection operations support Lists in index order and Objects in sorted key order. Query bindings are lexical for that query and are restored afterward. Statement `forEach` uses its declared iteration slots and executes its body for each selected item. An empty collection executes no iteration body. Map and flat-map produce Lists; flat-map requires a List result per item. Filter preserves the input's collection category. Reduce threads its accumulator. Some, find, and find-entry stop after the first decisive match. Find-entry preserves the selected value and occurrence information rather than replacing occurrence identity with value identity. Iteration gas is charged for each admitted visited item. Short-circuiting stops both later evaluation and later iteration charges. Collection construction retains its specified logical charges. Host memory/cancellation controls are operational and may interrupt without establishing a semantic rejection; they are not universal collection-size restrictions. ## 12. Variables, functions, and return `let` declares function-frame slots. Parallel declarations evaluate their initializers against the old frame; an explicit declaration order enables ordered dependency between initializers. `set` updates an existing declared slot. Conditional declaration visibility is checked statically. Function calls use isolated frames, exact declared argument-name sets, and supplied Blue argument-pattern checks. Functions share the invocation's effect accumulators and gas meter but do not implicitly capture another function's locals. Recursion is rejected during compilation. Business-process cycles therefore arise from Contracts event work, not recursive BEX function calls. Explicit return exits the current function/body. Without an explicit result, the interpreter returns the accumulated changeset and events. A called function's return does not terminate its caller. Failure exits the invocation and does not authorize partial publication. ## 13. Effects and host intrinsics Event append preserves multiplicity. Two equal event values are two emission occurrences; their BlueIds may be equal. Occurrence identity belongs to the hosting Contracts closure. The BEX interpreter does not deduplicate by content identity. An intrinsic must have an exact static type ID present in the invocation's installed capability registry. Unknown IDs fail compilation. Runtime removal of a capability fails execution. Intrinsics receive copied explicit operands and the same gas meter; they must return explicit BEX values and account for bounded work. Files, network, clock, and randomness are not implicit capabilities. ## 14. Gas Compilation consumes no semantic gas. Each admitted expression, statement, read, call, pointer operation, collection item, append, and size-dependent operation is charged by the algorithm at its specified point. A failed charge is recorded as rejected work and does not increment admitted `used` gas. Accepted charges update the running scalar only. They have no canonical rows, ordinals or transcript. Results contain `gas_used`, not `gas_trace`. The default standalone allowance remains 10,000,000. A caller-supplied shared meter is never reset; each invocation reports its own admitted contribution. Local counters and the shared total still enforce each charge before work. Retain only the first rejected charge, without a charge ordinal; a failed meter cannot resume accepting work. Optional debug traces are noncanonical, off by default, and never required for conformance, replay or durable publication. A compatibility API may expose an empty trace accessor, but this is not a result field in the new protocol. This is a new exact BEX edition. Earlier publications retain their original trace-bearing result and conformance rules; hosts must select those rules explicitly when replaying earlier histories. The default scalar tariffs are: expression 1; statement 1; document read 2; event/current-contract/steps/variable read 1; result-value read 2; pointer get base 1; pointer set base 3; object set base 2; append-change/event base 5; iteration item 1; function call 2. Size/path contributions are defined by the algorithms, not by wall-clock time. A Compute step can impose a positive local cap while charging each admitted operation to a shared Contracts closure meter. A local-cap rejection is distinguished from shared-cap rejection in the first-rejected-charge diagnostic. A cap is checked before work is admitted. Gas allowance, used gas, attempted rejected charge, and operational cancellation are different values. The charge positions and tariffs in the executable annex define this edition. A conforming implementation preserves the deterministic admitted gas total and first rejected charge for identical inputs. Equivalence to a different BEX release or another tariff is a separate interoperability claim, not an additional unstated rule. ## 15. Blue output boundary `blue_value` converts runtime values into a JSON-compatible, null-free proposal. It is not semantic admission and does not return a BlueId. Authoring aliases are resolved in an explicit authoring/preparation stage before this proposal enters the runtime output boundary. Runtime type slots MUST contain exact Blue references. The host admits the proposal through Language Exact admission and uses the resulting validated exact value; it MUST NOT resolve aliases, replay Source list construction, or reinterpret a generated string as an installed type at this stage. A BEX program may compute arbitrary Text, but a Text in a runtime type slot is not thereby a type reference. A host accepting raw data-encoded programs with unresolved literal type aliases must reject the resulting effect, not silently reinterpret it. The corrected boundary does not collapse null to `{}`. A whole null event or null patch value fails. Undefined object members may disappear, but required fields must still satisfy the host effect schema. Effect structural validation precedes mutation, so a later malformed effect cannot cause an earlier effect to be published. ## 16. Errors and determinism Compilation error, runtime error, invalid Blue output, actual gas exhaustion and host/incomplete execution are distinct failure families. The former portable resource caps are removed. Resource exceptions must propagate as incomplete host work, not be wrapped into ordinary BEX runtime failure and terminally rejected by a feeder. A caller may not turn an unavailable required Language definition or provider proof into a successful computation. A runtime exception never means "no changes" success. Determinism requires identical admitted inputs, program and definitions, installed capabilities, matcher behavior, selected document projection, and gas schedule. Python hash seed, input-map insertion order, cached parsing, and unrelated documents must not affect the semantic result. Stateful or nondeterministic intrinsics violate this requirement unless their observations are explicit frozen inputs. ## 17. Executable inventory and conformance the operator appendix lists every installed expression and statement operator. The complete annex supplies their compilation, evaluation, value and gas definitions. Each marked module is extracted without modification. The source table in this specification identifies the exact modules and their dependencies. Conformance preserves successful results, ordered proposals, short-circuit behavior, static errors, runtime errors, output-boundary errors and gas observations. Required cases include Boolean/Integer distinction; undefined/null/empty-object distinctions; exact arithmetic; type-pattern matching; every operator family; function scope; side-effect order; Unicode ordering and size; output rejection; and local/shared gas limits. Passing a finite corpus is evidence, not a proof for all programs or capabilities. ## 18. External capability boundary The standard algorithms require no arbitrary external I/O. A host supplies explicit document projections, a Language-backed matcher, and any selected intrinsic registry. A missing required capability or exact definition cannot be converted to successful evaluation. Intrinsics are trusted, explicitly installed code with their own semantics and bounded work; an unknown intrinsic ID is rejected. This edition defines no production network acquisition service, operating-system sandbox, universal intrinsic package or Java diagnostic mapping. An independent implementation conforms to this edition by preserving its specified results, not by reproducing an undocumented behavior of another runtime. Host memory protection and process isolation remain operational obligations; they cannot change the semantic outcome of an admitted computation. ## 19. Composition with Language and Contracts User-binding declarations are constants, functions, function arguments, local `$let` slots (both forms), and collection/loop item, key, index and accumulator slots. All reject the reserved names listed by `compiler.RESERVED`, including `$previousItems`. Ordinary literal object keys and host-provided read bindings are not user-binding declarations. `$previousItems` is a reserved Language name in BEX user-binding containers. It is not a BEX instruction and cannot manufacture Language list inheritance at runtime. `$previous` and other Source-only controls likewise do not replace Exact admission of effects. An unevaluated object containing dynamic expression fields is not an instance of its eventual result type. A repository can author that value through ordinary BEX `$objectFromEntries` construction with exact type references. Resulting events and patch values are admitted only after evaluation. Rewriting a program changes its identity and may change its gas; this does not weaken Language validation. The Contracts invocation supplies the selected executing document as the BEX document. BEX receives no ambient enclosing process or independently advancing public head. Contracts owns mutation boundaries, internal event occurrence identities, initialization, termination, checkpoint settlement, graph finalization and publication. BEX returns proposed effects and never advances those states itself. The standard Contracts binding uses its contextual business-value document projection for both `canonical` and `resolved` BEX read modes. This is an explicit Contracts binding, not a redefinition of the Language serialization APIs. Configured program data is distinct from effective business values: inherited specification prose must not be inserted into a literal program or effect. ## 20. Release and identity The complete specification comprises its readable rules, operator reference, executable algorithms and explicit dependency selection. Its BlueId names that exact Text. The publication manifest records its identity outside the Text, avoiding a self-reference. A normative change creates a new exact specification identity. Test reports, implementation-only packaging, tutorials and provenance notes do not silently amend this edition. ## 21. Immutable host values The numeric, equality, binding and control semantics are those defined in this specification. A trusted host may supply immutable collections implementing the host-value interface in values.py. Collection kind, keys, reads, variables, function arguments and persistent overlays operate on these values without eager recursive cloning. Output conversion uses the host's finite exact representation. The host must bind coherent resolution and meter demanded work. `$fail` and `$failIf` expose the distinct EXECUTION_REJECTED diagnostic so a host can classify explicit business rejection without treating every BEX error as a user refusal. Arithmetic and control tariffs are defined by the executable gas module. Collection equality keeps its ordered short-circuit comparisons. A host can provide a stable comparison key for an exact effective recipe in its captured context. Repeated pairs in a cyclic comparison need not be unfolded again; unrelated fields and unequal pairs remain observable. Equality must not eagerly read the remaining values after a decisive mismatch. ## 22. Shared host metering When invoked by Contracts, BEX uses the same bounded meter: **10,000,000 maximum/default** for the complete Contracts attempt, with supported stricter local limits. No BEX frame, intrinsic, compiled-program cache or lower standalone-Gas setting can detach from or reset the parent meter. Standalone BEX API budget configuration remains a separate API contract; it cannot enlarge the standard Contracts allowance. Work charges apply independently of physical resource controls. Conversion, Integer arithmetic, collections, strings and output sizing use the exact counters, quantities and charge positions defined here. Implementations MUST NOT substitute after-the-fact bit-length caps or wall-clock timeouts for the specified meter. Any changed tariff requires a separately identified specification and conformance vectors. Preserve ordinary validation failure order and short-circuit behavior; no charges execute in an unselected branch. Compiler structure checks remain semantically complete, including unused branches and forbidden recursive functions. Compilation still consumes no BEX semantic gas under this schedule; any inability to finish compilation is a prerequisite/host failure, not a fabricated failed debit. This rule neither exempts the containing Contracts work from its existing charges nor makes first-time authoring free in physical resources. ## 23. Resource-proportional work accounting Contracts continues to supply one shared meter with a maximum of 10000000. BEX compilation and host prerequisite acquisition are outside that invocation meter. A host interruption is incomplete execution, never a BEX semantic rejection. Three additional BEX counters have unit weight 1: `integerWork`, `textWork`, and `valueMember`. They are charged to the current invoking member before their corresponding work. Let L(n) = max(1, ceil(bit_length(abs(n))/32)). Addition and subtraction debit max(L(a),L(b)); multiplication debits L(a)*L(b); division debits 2*L(a)*L(b), before the zero/exact-division check and arithmetic. """ from concurrent.futures import CancelledError from asyncio import CancelledError as AsyncCancelledError from functools import wraps class HostIncomplete(Exception): code = 'HOST_INCOMPLETE' def __init__(self, reason, **context): self.reason = reason self.context = {'reason': reason, **context} super().__init__(reason) HOST_FAILURES = (HostIncomplete, MemoryError, RecursionError, CancelledError, AsyncCancelledError) def incomplete(error): if isinstance(error, HostIncomplete): return error return HostIncomplete(type(error).__name__) def host_boundary(fn): """Convert incidental host failures without manufacturing an Outcome.""" @wraps(fn) def run(*args, **kwargs): try: return fn(*args, **kwargs) except HOST_FAILURES as error: raise incomplete(error) from error return run ``` ### Source inventory | Module | SHA-256 of supplied UTF-8 file | |---|---| | `src/blue_bex/__init__.py` | `820ef8825a174b5f9666b9b713d51e20bcf8fa6c509b79128fb373433033e8d8` | | `src/blue_bex/compiler.py` | `6af97e5067510b862cbb0edc808fc7903f4f0be51c8ff45a31df07be9bdfa55d` | | `src/blue_bex/gas.py` | `78cb48147d907a6b84535563d5dddd543b6bf734447a184e7a50b49b5cc42803` | | `src/blue_bex/runtime.py` | `171ad8489e317d2a22326649e88fa64a8a45461d5956850c6d5080cd997c9b65` | | `src/blue_bex/values.py` | `59fc4bee80e54e5e9d64824ee18aed8a195220137f0eaaf5f1e58adb11951b8a` | | `src/blue_host/__init__.py` | `ac30b5090d56b101150b3bdb9bb05fff265308737c3ea0dd8b9caa22b0b5b607` | "}

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Contracts — demand-scoped execution edition

**Status:** normative candidate rules for a local experimental publication; not a qualified release or an implemented conformance claim.
**Proposed edition:** `blue-contracts/2026-10-22-demand-scoped-1`.
**Proposed package version:** `1.0.0-demand-scoped.1`; final release metadata is assigned by the canonical build owner.
**Baseline:** [final-gas specification](contracts-final-gas.md).
**Conformance and implementation gates:** [demand-scoped cases](contracts-demand-scoped-conformance.md).

The canonical build assigns the candidate BlueIds from these exact rules and their pinned imports. Prior archived publications and existing specifications remain unchanged. This candidate may be built locally to bind and test the new implementation; it MUST NOT become a production default or a qualified release until the linked conformance gates and normal lifecycle tests pass. Sections 12.1–12.5 define the replacement algorithms and take precedence over the baseline's conflicting whole-certification and whole-closure calls; baseline scheduling and unrelated semantics remain unchanged. The candidate label is not evidence that D1–D5 have passed.

## 1. Contract and compatibility

The new edition defines successful execution as completion of every obligation required by the requested Contracts transition, including its required evidence retention. It does not certify every value transitively reachable from its input, event or result. Blue Language remains the authority for exact identity, effective types, constraints, exact evidence and cyclic proof validation. `strict_certify`/`NativeRuntime.strict` retain their full meaning.

The public cause remains the original exact event and supplied timestamp. Channel Event Checkpoint retains `event: {blueId: ORIGINAL_EVENT_ID}`. Event bytes, signatures and predecessor links MUST NOT be rewritten. This edition introduces neither `entryId` nor `eventProofs`, serialized coverage certificates, external completion tokens or new trusted claims in document content.

All prior editions retain their original processing, certification, gas and storage rules. An exact installed edition binding selects this policy before a request executes; availability, account age, author-supplied labels and cache state cannot select it. New and old account runtimes may coexist in one process without sharing edition-dependent conclusions. Cross-edition processing of one managed document is outside this release.

Unless explicitly revised here, retain the final-gas edition's operation selection, deterministic scheduling, protected markers, occurrence identities, lifecycle, generalization, failure observations and public API. Coordination determines signed source validity, authority, history and admission under its separately selected edition; Contracts does not infer these from an event-shaped value.

## 2. One obligation policy

An invocation has a private working context and an obligation set. An obligation identifies:

```
(edition, input snapshot, original cause, current exact member/view,
 contextual Recipe, processor role, operation/purpose, required coverage)
```

The tuple is a semantic identity, not a required new serialized format. Coverage denotes what was established: exact identity/evidence, effective header, contextual predicate, selected value/subtree, managed occurrence, or complete Language value/definition. These categories MUST NOT be treated as interchangeable trust levels. A contextual predicate fact is not a whole-value certificate, even when its exact BlueId equals a completely certified value in another role.

The native processor and the actual operation determine obligations. Source availability MUST NOT change their meaning. A successful full-content execution and a successful missing-unused-content execution on the same source MUST have identical observations and logical gas. A required missing record produces `NEEDS_RESOURCES`; invalid evidence produces the native validation error; unsupported semantics produces an explicit failure, never a successful filter mismatch or a false absence.

Obligations are extended by actual observations and writes. Conditional BEX evaluation adds obligations for its discriminant and selected branch under normal BEX semantics. An unselected branch does not acquire an execution obligation merely because it is reachable. Metadata and constraints may nevertheless require inspecting it. This rule does not allow the processor to ignore an already established obligation when a resource is unavailable.

There is no exemption set keyed only by BlueId. The same exact body may be opaque predecessor data and a required current operand. The latter role MUST perform its own contextual validation and demand missing content. Repeated obligations may reuse verified facts only when their complete context and coverage agree; metering follows the logical work rule, not physical reuse.

## 3. Native observations and contextual validity

The current Java interfaces provide building blocks, not a ready-made general scoped certificate:

| Operation | Actual interface | Meaning and restriction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact root/evidence | `NativeRuntime.identity`, `NativeRuntime.open`; `RuntimeBridge.open` | Exact record and owning proof are verified when opened. A hash/reference alone does not establish type validity. |
| Effective contextual header | `NativeRuntime.head/readHead(Recipe, runtime)` | Preserve effective type, inherited contributions, requirements and metadata. A header is not a full certificate. |
| Descendant selection | `NativeRuntime.child(Head, key)`; `RuntimeBridge.child/select` | Derive the child from the effective parent Recipe; do not replace it with a standalone reference that loses `valueType`, `itemType` or inherited requirements. |
| Contextual whole subtree | `NativeRuntime.validate(Recipe, runtime, goal)` | Validates that selected subtree using Language semantics. It may demand descendants; it is not a partial-validation flag. |
| Containing constraints | `runtime.validateConstraints(Head, root)` | Run native constraints against the actual effective head. Constraint evaluation may demand more content. This call alone does not check every metadata, type or structural obligation. |
| Native type/definition | `NativeRuntime.ancestry/subtype`, `NativeRuntime.strict(...,"definition")` where whole definition is required | Do not replace native subtype, fixed-value, specification or schema logic with string/type-name checks. |
| Scalar observation | `RuntimeBridge.project` on the selected Recipe | Projection consumes a value; its result must not be hashed as the original exact identity. |
| Full certificate | `NativeRuntime.strict` / `RuntimeBridge.certify` | Unchanged complete Language check; only actual successful full checks may populate its cache. |

Every operation that observes a node MUST establish the validity of the information it uses, including the containing constraints that govern that observation. Own and inherited type/schema, `specification`, fixed values, labels, merge policy and container metadata are not optional simply because the selected descendant is otherwise well typed. Requiredness, presence and absence are resolved through the effective parent; unavailable evidence is not absence.

A processor MAY defer a child's value validation only if neither its action nor a governing predicate requires that value. It MUST still check governing predicates that apply at its selected container boundary. For example, an invalid `maxFields` on `contracts` cannot be bypassed by validating each contract separately. A `valueType` constraint on `count` cannot be discharged by certifying the number outside its parent. A specification reference required for the selected node must resolve and validate with Language's definition semantics.

The lowering of each native handler into these obligations MUST be listed and tested. If a Language predicate requires the entire subtree, invoke that native predicate with the required evidence; do not substitute a structural guess. If the existing interfaces cannot express a necessary selected predicate without imposing unrelated full validation, record an executable reproducer and an explicit API/design decision before publication. This draft does not authorize altering Language or BEX semantics or introducing a global skip-validation switch.

### 3.1 First bounded lowering: required containers

The initial additive Java primitive observes an already-required object or list container. It does not decide optional-child presence and is not a replacement for complete snapshot validation. It verifies authored and effective type/specification/item/key/value metadata through native definition checks. For an empty effective constraint description, there is no constraint predicate to evaluate: after explicit required-container shape checks, this lowering does not call the native constraint routine's incidental concrete-child counting. A nonempty effective constraint continues through native evaluation and may widen the demand, except for the required-object presence lowering below. This is a Contracts obligation/gas-plan decision, not a change to Language strict validation.

A container/header obligation MUST retain its original contextual Recipe and discharge its governing definitions. After constructing the native effective Head and establishing presence using the existing native occurrence/root rules, it MAY discharge the effective constraint without native object-field counting if and only if the Head kind is `object`, the checked occurrence is present, and the effective constraints description contains exactly `required` with a Boolean value. The required-presence predicate is then satisfied; no field-count predicate exists. This MUST still charge the existing `schemaPredicateEvaluated` obligation for `required` and MUST NOT establish a whole-value certificate or reusable value obligation.

Absent occurrences, scalar/list/none kinds, and every other effective constraint combination MUST continue through native validation. Inherited constraints are part of the effective description. In particular, `minFields`, `maxFields`, key/value/item rules and required scalar/list payload checks MUST NOT be bypassed. Governing metadata and observed ordinary records retain their existing obligations. Native presence remains authoritative: an object-shaped definition alone is not a present value. Legacy validation and tariffs are unchanged.

Canonical key validation is currently exposed only through whole native subtree validation. The first primitive therefore widens a container with explicit `keyType` to complete selected validation; it does not claim lazy `keyType` support or duplicate Language's key parser. Actual selected-value use performs full selected exact certification plus the contextual Recipe validation, preserving parent `itemType`/`valueType` requirements. Neither the container observation nor its return value is stored as a full certificate. These restrictions remain explicit until tested lowering is expanded.

### 3.2 Handler requirements

Discovery reads the effective contract map, keys, runtime type ancestry, ordering and fields used to classify/route a declaration. It MUST NOT project or certify an entire workflow merely to identify its handler. The exact installed runtime catalogue supplies the handler policy; business document IDs and workflow IDs do not.

Before an eligible handler executes, validate its consumed declaration fields, filter and selected step under their contextual Recipes. Filters preserve native presence, refinement and constraint semantics; only proven mismatch returns false. A request schema or authorization predicate that requires a payload makes that payload required. The same applies to ordinary observers: operation routing is not an exemption from an observer's actual reads.

Initial supported handler policies MUST be derived from the actual Order, Activation and mandate primitive inventory. Adding a recognized custom runtime without a defined obligation policy MUST fail explicitly, not inherit a permissive policy. This is a runtime capability rule, not a business whitelist.

## 4. Boundary obligations

| Boundary | Mandatory obligations | Deferred content |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh input | Source/exact identity; reject forged protected markers; effective managed shape, declaration discovery and initialization requirements | Unselected workflow bodies/branches except where governing constraints require them |
| Snapshot restore | Closed envelope, expected and recomputed commitment, release/bindings, exact member roots and cyclic ownership, root/edge/lifetime/serial/marker integrity, contextual structural constraints | Unused ordinary descendants and historical event operands; no blanket full-body fact |
| Event ingress | Original exact event identity, supplied timestamp, contextual fields needed by dispatch and applicable constraints; signed admission remains host responsibility | Predecessor payload/foreign operand content not required by this action |
| Channel/checkpoint | Native marker type and applicable contextual constraints, channel lifetime, exact event reference, timestamp scalar/range and native channel progression rules | Reachable history not consumed by these checks |
| Handler/BEX | Selected declaration/step, current read operands, native filter and required parameter constraints, captured view/resolver and logical meter | Unselected branch bodies and untouched value descendants |
| Patch | Native construction, selected path and target context, protected-state/generalization rules, constraints affected by the write, reconciled graph/occurrences | Unchanged subtrees only where their governing obligations are unaffected |
| Finalization | All outstanding local/graph obligations, stable identities and cyclic proofs, sealed source state, pending reactions and required retention | No obligation may be silently dropped at this boundary |
| Completion/receive | Local verified origin, before/after views, cause, edition/bindings, complete execution-unit membership, tickets and exact predecessor compatibility | No assumption of whole-value certification from a valid completion |
| Export/cold restore | Exact retained records and owning proofs sufficient to reconstruct the specified restore/receive obligations; expected commitments | Optional unused closure must not leak through inline ancestors |

A patch changing a type, schema, specification, container structure or managed declaration invalidates dependent obligations. Re-evaluate them on the new contextual view before the next step observes it. Do not reuse the unchanged child BlueId's old contextual result when its parent requirements changed. The existing native generalization and constraint rules remain authoritative; preservation of their effects must be demonstrated rather than replaced by post-hoc acceptance.

Identity-only observation must remain identity-only even for an inline body. Real scalar/subtree access must perform the same contextual work for inline and referenced forms. Reading a checkpoint timestamp through native projection is legitimate; rewriting its persisted representation or relaxing integer checks is not.

## 5. Invocation and publication algorithm

The following pseudocode specifies ordering and invariants. `require_for` is a proposed internal obligation operation, not an existing Language API. Its handler-specific lowering and the complete executable reference implementation are release gates.

```
execute(edition, input, originalEvent, time):
    assert installed exact edition/bindings
    tx := fork input state, Language evidence context, obligation facts,
               archive updates, completion registrations and retained output
    require_for(tx, RESTORE_OR_INPUT, input)
    require_for(tx, EVENT_DISPATCH, originalEvent, time)
    run existing deterministic Contracts scheduling in tx
        before each observation: require_for(tx, selected contextual role)
        before installing each patch: native construct/generalize and
            require_for(tx, affected contextual write obligations)
        after patch: reconcile and finalize required local/graph obligations
    require_for(tx, FINALIZE, resulting managed graph)
    retained := prepare_required_records(tx, input, result, originalEvent)
    verify retained records can satisfy cold restore and local receive obligations
    seal outcome and its cause/edition/member bindings
    atomically install tx context, stable state, retained output, archive and
        process-local completion establishment
    return APPLIED
on missing, invalid, exhausted or incomplete execution/required retention:
    discard tx effects, evidence additions, selected facts and registrations
    return the edition's failure/incomplete result against original input
```

Preparing retention is part of success, not an optional operation after completion establishment. A late export failure cannot leave a newly capturable result, advanced checkpoint, archive entry or reusable selected fact behind. Preserve previous prepared/committed output. Repeating the exact input/event/time after obtaining the required evidence runs against the original stable input and does not duplicate a previously partial mutation.

This local atomic boundary is distinct from durable host publication. The host's existing journal transaction MUST atomically publish the completed state/evidence, original cause, progress, emitted effects and retry obligations. A transient local result is not evidence of durable commit. Host failure cannot publish a receipt/progress record without its required content. This draft does not require a new journal or service.

## 6. Completion guarantee and normal receiving

A new-edition completion establishes: this installed edition executed the identified input and original cause through all required obligations, obtained the exact resulting managed state and ordered output, and prepared all evidence required by this completion's storage/receive contract. It does NOT assert complete Language validity of every transitively reachable value.

Preserve the existing local capability boundary:

1. Only the actual successful local attempt may establish an outcome; bind input snapshot identity, event BlueId/timestamp, release, exact runtime bindings, before/after member views, receipt, units and ordered effects.
2. `capture` requires that established local outcome and matching process-local provenance. Validate selected members, owner birth rules and complete unit inclusion. A user-provided receipt, after-body or matching hash is insufficient.
3. `receive`/live receive verifies issuer, capability lifetime, cause, compatible exact edition/bindings, owned members, captured occurrence tickets and predecessor views. It validates its own contextual obligations. Incorporation is not full certification of the source's opaque closure.
4. Process restart does not deserialize a trusted capability from input bytes. The installed privileged local `CompletionReader` may recover an atomically committed local completion, verify descriptor/receipt and bindings, restore required before/after evidence under this edition, and re-establish local provenance. Arbitrary imported snapshots cannot invoke this path.
5. Modified, foreign, expired, overlapping or incompatible completion records remain rejected. This edition does not define public third-party execution proofs.

The existing descriptor's `release`, `runtimes`, before/after vectors, event, timestamp and receipt carry these bindings; there is no new user-authored coverage flag. Changing an edition changes its immutable specification identity and therefore its interpretation. The reference implementation MUST explicitly apply the new guarantee at establishment and rehydration; deleting `UNESTABLISHED_SOURCE_COMPLETION` is not an implementation.

## 7. Retention, privacy and cyclic exact content

Compute required records from the obligation roles and replay/restore requirements, not from whatever extra content happens to be cached. A record may be required in one role even if another role defers the same BlueId. Retaining unused private bodies because they were available in the full-control runtime violates deterministic scoped export/privacy.

For acyclic exact records, preserve exact identity while emitting finite child references; verify identity after serialization. Traversal follows the required roles. Do not serialize an inline ancestor wholesale when it contains an excluded descendant. A missing excluded descendant is not replaced by null, empty content or a fabricated value.

For a cyclic member, retain and verify the Language owning-set proof and required member body using the existing canonical proof/body mechanism. Do not emit an ordinary acyclic `mode: exact` record under `master#i`. Deduplicate with a finite identity/context/role work set, not by dropping owning proofs or globally whitelisting an identity. Historical graph edges such as A(T) → B(T) → A(T−1) remain exact historical edges, not latest-state aliases.

Cold restore opens and verifies actual supplied exact records and owning proofs, then derives the required obligations anew under the selected edition. Serialized statements of prior validation are not trusted. Missing content needed for these obligations must still wait/fail. Record presence or prior selective success cannot seed complete closure caches, `RuntimeBridge.certified`, or full Language validation caches.

The primitive inventory must identify actual cycles used by Order/Activation. There is no global cycle prohibition. If a required cycle cannot be retained privately with valid owning evidence, report that concrete case and resolve its contract before claiming qualification.

## 8. Logical work

Preserve the existing logical tariff operations and deterministic ordering where applicable. The new edition charges the logical observations and validations defined by its obligation plan, independently of fetch count, cache warmth, inline/reference encoding and retry timing. Reusing evidence does not erase a required charge. A selected obligation ledger is not a full-certificate cache.

The old edition's all-descendant `LogicalWork.visit` cannot automatically be the new policy's walk: it may traverse deliberately unselected data. Before release, specify the traversal for each handler's obligation and its deduplication context in the executable metering appendix. Record any intentional new-edition gas difference; old A/B gas remains exact. Experimental values 569, 645 and 708 are measured comparisons for old bindings inside the overlay, not golden totals for the new publication.

## 9. Coordination interface and unresolved release gates

Contracts accepts the original cause and supplied time. Coordination is responsible for signed prefix verification, authority, receiver history, Q06 routing, Q13 catch-up and durable scheduling. Skipping an unrelated operation is not a synthetic Contracts checkpoint. An ordinary observer can independently require event content. No new global `unknown => NO_MATCH` rule is introduced here.

The companion [receiver-relative replay draft](../../blue-coordination/spec/receiver-relative-replay-draft.md) requires child-only historical catch-up from its original raw source and own initialization, including the birth cause, without reseeding the creating parent. Contracts must preserve exact occurrence generations, source member provenance and complete execution-unit boundaries when receiving those results. Equal standalone/embedded document state does not authorize adopting a completion from a different member origin. The caller must supply the original admitted event and frozen history context; no artificial event wrapper or fabricated checkpoint substitutes for them. Concrete owner/subgraph eligibility and same-order dependency-cycle handling require the agreed executable Coordination/Contracts composition before qualification.

The following are explicit open implementation/specification gates, not permissions to weaken checks:

- **D1 contextual lowering:** enumerate actual Order/Activation/mandate handlers; map own/inherited metadata and parent constraints to native operations. Prove unselected workflow/branch remains unopened when no governing predicate requires it. If current API cannot express this, first produce the specific failing case and proposed API contract.
- **D2 normal completion:** update reference establishment/retention/rehydration algorithms and exercise receiving dependent work plus journal restart. Existing overlay capture refusal remains historical evidence, not a new-edition expectation.
- **D3 cyclic transport:** use genuine owning proof/body export for all required cyclic sets; test inline and referenced variants and malformed proofs. The experimental blanket `#` rejection is not carried forward.
- **D4 gas:** specify selected logical traversal, then qualify full/missing and warm/cold equivalence without normalizing observations.
- **D5 Coordination agreement:** finalize recipient/history/birth rules with the new Coordination specification. Contracts laziness alone does not solve unknown nonexact targets or raw-child history equality.

## 10. Carry / replace / retire

| Carry into production requirements/tests | Replace in the new edition | Retain only as historical experiment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact refs/commitments, contextual Recipe, role aliasing, native errors, fork rollback, full/missing equivalence, original signatures, scalar projection | Whole-root restore/certification assumptions with declared obligations; full closure export with verified required-record retention; edition dispatch and normal completion guarantee | Compiler string replacements, child-first shadow classes, trace hooks, one count type/workflow whitelist, plain-container rejection, global cyclic rejection, suppressed archive/completion |
| Actual run97407 mutation-before-missing, one-record retry, strict-matched replay and gas | Hand-inserted evidence in acceptance with authorized provider delivery and durable wake/restart | Run97407 is not signed Order/network qualification |
| Existing old-edition A/B exact state/gas/receipt/terminal decisions and old RED tests | New publication and new-account binding after qualification | Do not edit old expected Q13 difference or relabel old failures PASS |
