The actual generated run97407 sources were inspected: six native copies plus `PartialSnapshotReconstructionExperiment` and `PartialCounterOverlaySession`. Their selected helper pins one exact type, rejects unsupported metadata, suppresses normal completion, and rejects cyclic records. The new implementation must replace these restrictions with the declared handler obligations, not simply remove the guards.

## 12. Source-based implementation algorithms for the next vertical slice

This section makes D2–D4 implementable without treating pseudocode identifiers as existing APIs. These algorithms are the proposed new-edition behavior. They remain subject to executable reference/Java equivalence tests; old-edition branches retain their current algorithms.

### 12.1 Restoration and event preparation

```
restore_required(package, expected, installedPolicy):
    check closed package/snapshot metadata and expected/recomputed commitment
    check exact release and supported runtime binding vector
    fork Language context; stage package.content in that fork
    construct member/edge metadata using existing ContractStorage.restore parsing
    for each exact member root:
        open native exact body/owning proof
        observe required container and its governing metadata
        discover effective managed contracts without demanding handler bodies
        check protected markers in their effective parent context
        check channel lifetime signatures/serials and initialized requirements
        check declared occurrence paths, target exact identity and edge generations
    return immutable reconstructed Snapshot plus staged verified evidence
on error: discard fork, restore caller evidence and all restore facts
```

This does not invoke or populate the old `restore-body` fact. Edge identity checks in `ContractGraph.verifyEdges` remain, but the new branch invokes the declared structural obligations instead of unconditional whole `blue.certify(d.body)`. The same structural validator is used at process input and cold restore. A direct selected child MUST NOT bypass ancestor-container checks: selection retains the ancestor chain/role, and the policy checks each required container before consuming the child's contextual Recipe. A child Recipe carries its value requirements, not every ancestor's cardinality predicate.

Event preparation opens the original exact event and invokes the dispatcher obligation rather than `RuntimeBridge.node(... certify=true)` on its entire history. `ContractChannels.recognize` and effective operation/filter discovery consume their declared fields. Before using any actual operand they invoke the contextual value obligation. Unknown ordinary event types are not silently marked valid: their applicable metadata and each consuming observer/filter determine native obligations. Signed proof validation stays in Coordination.

Checkpoint validation consumes type/entries/channel/timestamp/event identity under their ancestor constraints. The native timestamp projection is used for referenced and inline scalar representations alike. An event identity stored in a checkpoint does not obligate traversal of its predecessor payload. A later read through that same Ref does.

### 12.2 Run transaction, normal establishment and receiving

Use the existing `ContractRun` state copy and `NativeRuntime.fork`, not a second executor. The new-edition invocation owner retains the previous context, archive changes, completion registrations and obligation ledger. All synchronous process and chunked/receiving entry points must use this owner; a successful synchronous-only test does not qualify chunk paths.

```
finish_required(run):
    graph.finalizeGraph()
    preflight required structural/runtime obligations
    set revision/generation under existing transition rules
    validate required final graph obligations
    construct Outcome with normal events/work/checkpoints/turns/rounds/units/gas
    prepared := prepare_records(input, output, event, required views, obligations)
    verify prepared exact records and required restore/receive completeness
    seal Outcome using existing immutable observations/receipt calculation
    commit invocation context and prepared records
    archive.add(final state)
    completions.remember(input, Outcome, original event ID, timestamp)
    return normal Result
```

Replace only the new branch of `ContractRun.finishWork`'s unconditional full `blue.retain` with `prepare_records`; do not suppress `archive.add` or `completions.remember`. Preparation MUST complete before either observable registration. No failure-capable external I/O belongs between publication of a local completion and its required local record preparation. If registration itself fails, undo the invocation's registrations and context; do not retain a half-established outcome. Existing capability FIFO/lifetime and unit ownership checks remain.

A normal `capture` calls the existing `ContractCompletions.capture` against the successful local establishment. Receiving calls existing `run/install` and checks exact before-views, source-unit membership, causes and compatible binding vectors; its own obligations run inside the same transaction boundary. Source state adoption does not establish complete certificates for untouched payloads.

On cold local completion recovery, the installed `CompletionReader` supplies before/after packages plus immutable observations/receipt and original event/time from its committed local journal. Restore both packages with the new structural validator; verify receipt/status/input/cause/release/bindings; only then call existing local establishment and capture. The trusted-reader installation, not the serialized descriptor, proves local origin. This remains distinct from arbitrary portable invocation import.

The durable host writes prepared records, result, event cause and history/progress/effects in its existing publication transaction. Content demand failures leave durable wait state, not a committed failed intermediate execution. The owner must not accidentally restore the previous context for one entry point but retain it for `receive`, portable import or chunk finalization.

### 12.3 Required records and genuine cyclic proof/body

The required-record worklist contains `(exact node, contextual Recipe and ancestor obligations, role, retention purpose)` derived from structural restore/receive requirements and actual invocation obligations.

Transport preparation also retains ordinary records for local-free exact Values actually constructed during this invocation and the required evidence of its actual emitted outputs. Construction capture is scoped to newly constructed Values and their established exact identities; it MUST NOT enumerate provider inventory, traverse explicit Refs or certify future referenced payloads. These records use the same native shallow-record/owning-proof preparation as other required transport. Invocation forks copy this pending retention state; successful finish merges it into prepared content before sealing and publication, while failed or abandoned work drops it. Preparing exact evidence for actual emitted outputs does not add a second logical tariff or a new completion authority. This is produced-content retention, not a demand for every possible future handler body.

The required-record worklist is not a snapshot of all available resolver evidence and not a full Language closure walk. Each role defines which child edges are required; actual consumed values and governing definitions include their required validation dependencies. A bare original event reference remains present without forcing unused payload edges.

```
prepare_records(roots, obligation roles):
    todo := deterministic required roots/roles
    seen := empty set of (identity, role, purpose)
    records := empty exact-record map
    while todo not empty:
        (node, role, purpose) := next deterministic obligation
        if already seen: continue
        body := NativeRuntime.open(node)            # verifies actual exact evidence
        requiredChildren := role.requiredEdges(body, contextual obligations)
        if ordinary exact identity:
            shallow := replace immediate Exact children/items by same-identity Refs
            require native identity(shallow) == native identity(body)
            record := existing {mode: exact, text: exactText(shallow)} format
        else cyclic member:
            original := runtime.evidence()[memberID]
            require genuine verified owning proof exists in original
            record := {proof: original.proof, body: exactText(shallow body)}
            queue native verification in the fresh checking context below
            # A cyclic member ID is checked by its proof, not identity(body)==memberID.
        records[identity(node)] := prospective record
        enqueue requiredChildren with their contextual Recipes/ancestor obligations
    check := fresh NativeRuntime with ONLY records plus explicitly declared public package records
    verify/open all prospective records in check using native evidence verification
    verify no required record/proof auxiliary is omitted
    return records
```

The existing Java evidence API is sufficient to investigate this without exporting a complete closure: `NativeRuntime.evidence()` exposes retained `Map` records; an internal `ExactResponse` exposes the same canonical `proof/body` wire fields; `NativeRuntime.open` and `verifyEvidence` verify evidence; `finalizeComponent` already stores genuine owning proofs. Do not access private Language caches reflectively or construct a replacement proof algorithm. `NativeRuntime.records`/`retain` are intentionally complete closure operations and cannot substitute for this worklist.

Verification in the producer context is insufficient: `verifyEvidence` inherits its provider and can conceal omitted auxiliaries. The fresh checker MUST NOT inherit producer state, validation facts or nonpublic evidence.

The cyclic branch MUST be tested against a real `finalizeComponent` result and an imported proof/body record. The prospective shallow body must pass native owning-proof verification. If a retained canonical owning proof itself contains private data that cannot be removed without changing the proof, this is a concrete representational conflict to report, not permission to redact a proof or omit it. No claim of cycle support is made solely from this pseudocode. Canonical list/previous auxiliaries required by the selected Language encoding must be retained as part of evidence validity; comparing only the top-level hash is insufficient.

### 12.4 Deterministic role edges

The following table defines the initial obligations. A transition to a child retains its contextual `Recipe` and the enclosing container obligations. Enumeration uses native field order and list index order. Availability, a resolver hit, and a previously imported complete certificate MUST NOT choose a role.

| Boundary | Required observations | Deferred edges until their consumer runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Snapshot member | Exact root, native required object container, governing definitions, contracts container, graph declarations, marker headers and lifetime fields | Ordinary state values not read by these observations; checkpoint event payload/history |
| Contracts map | Required container and each declaration's type/role, specification compatibility, allowed field names, ordering/channel/embedding headers | Native `BODY` fields of unselected declarations |
| Sequential Workflow / Operation header | `channel`, `event` or `request` filter, `order`; existence and list shape of `steps` | Step bodies before selection |
| Selected step | Exact declaration type and governing definitions; step parameters as the existing handler consumes them | BEX operands represented by a view until the corresponding BEX operation consumes a value |
| Checkpoint | Native checkpoint type/ancestry and contextual predicates, timestamp Integer, original event exact identity | Original event children not consumed by event dispatch or a handler |
| Event dispatch | Required event container, applicable governing definitions, channel selection fields and each selected filter | Nonselected payload and history branches; an explicit filter traversal removes the deferral |
| BEX child lookup | Enclosing required container and requested key/index; preserve the child Recipe | Child value until its operation needs value semantics; BlueId observation requires exact identity only |
| Mutation | Constructed value, changed contextual value and every enclosing container; graph/marker/lifetime invariants | Unchanged branches unless governing predicates or the selected handler consume them |
| Completion/receive | Same structural obligations on exact before/after members, original cause, edition/runtime compatibility, units, provenance and local capability checks | Unconsumed original cause graph; no receiving-time inference that a selected fact is whole certification |

For the native declaration roles, body fields are exactly: workflow/operation `steps`; compute `expr do constants functions entry definition`; compute-definition `constants functions`; patch-step `changeset`; emit-step `event`; terminate-step `cause reason`. All other declared fields are header fields. `specification` is a governing definition, not an ignored body field. Existing native allowed-field and required-field checks still apply. Installed extensions use their exact edition-bound `headerFields`/`bodyFields`; selecting an extension requires its declared body operands before invocation unless that extension's own normative specification defines finer contextual reads. An unknown extension cannot inherit a native role's deferrals.

BEX program and literal/constant projection preserves two distinct inputs: the original authored exact data and its contextual Recipe. Authored fields determine the existing BEX data shape; inherited type fields MUST NOT be materialized as authored literal properties. Literal data uses a definition-header observation under the contextual Recipe, and a native scalar value uses contextual value validation. The program-syntax scalar-definition fallback first constructs the effective Head, then validates the authored Exact node with the native definition goal; this is not a claim of full contextual definition certification for that fallback. Program syntax is read as syntax; `$literal` is an opaque data boundary until a consumer reads it. A native scalar value uses its value obligation, while a scalar definition without a value uses native definition semantics rather than being treated as an absent runtime scalar. This preserves the existing authored-data projection and definition/value distinction; it does not remove metadata or permit deferred executable syntax.

Required-resource provenance includes actual native opens performed by the selected matcher, not only reads through an `ExactView` wrapper. The invocation-local matcher collector records bodies actually opened by that evaluation and relates its reported missing identities to ordinary authored edges in those bodies. It does not search provider inventory, infer authored paths from type inheritance or establish source authority. The host still requires the existing authenticated/adopted source provenance before fetching a missing identity. A native validation failure remains a failure; only the native mismatch categories may become a false match.

A required native filter uses native matching predicates and contextual constraints. A field-only positive matcher is not permitted. If the current native API cannot evaluate a predicate without a broader required subtree, that broader subtree is a required obligation and can produce `NEEDS_RESOURCES`; it must not be accepted based on a partial predicate. Likewise, explicit `keyType` currently widens to native full contextual validation rather than a replacement key parser. These widening rules are based on predicate/role, not content availability.

### 12.5 Logical obligation traversal and reuse

This edition introduces a separate obligation ledger; it does not change the old edition's `LogicalWork.validate/visit` algorithm or select behavior by broadening `finalGas()`. One attempt owns the ledger and meter. A chunk continuation copies both; an independent attempt or cold processor starts a new ledger. Failed fork work cannot publish facts or completion, even when its returned diagnostic reports gas already consumed.

The ledger key is `(contextual Recipe.key, obligation kind, coverage)`. Kinds are `container`, `definition`, and `value`; coverage identifies the complete selected contextual subtree for `value`, and the observed container/predicate/header set for `container`. Ancestor observations have their own keys. An unchanged BlueId under a different Recipe or coverage is a distinct obligation. Container/definition success never establishes a value key. Global Language/bridge caches do not affect this logical ledger.

The reference algorithm is:

```text
require(obligation):
    first require each enclosing container in outermost-to-innermost order
    if this exact obligation key succeeded in this invocation:
        charge validationProofReused once
        return its previously established obligation result
    dispatch by kind using the algorithms below
    record success only after the native check succeeds
```

For `container`, open each authored Recipe part through `LogicalWork.open` (which charges `nodeManifestOpened` once per exact ID per invocation), construct the unchanged native effective Head, and follow its applicable governing definitions with `definition` obligations. Each type edge followed charges `typeEdgeFollowed`; each explicitly selected ordinary child edge charges `objectMemberRead`, or `listItemRead` for an index. Charge `schemaPredicateEvaluated` once for each key of the effective constraints' `describe()` map, in sorted-key order. Perform the native required-container check and native effective predicate evaluation, subject only to the required-object presence lowering in §3.1: an effective object occurrence established present by native rules, with exactly the Boolean `required` constraint, discharges that predicate without incidental field counting while retaining its predicate charge. Empty effective constraints have zero predicate charges and no concrete-count walk. Incidental resolver/cache work inside the native predicate implementation is physical work, not a second logical traversal or a whole-subtree value charge. Predicate-driven widening invokes an explicit `value` obligation, whose own charges are separate; it cannot silently establish a value certificate from the container result.

For `definition`, traverse the exact definition evidence needed by native definition certification in deterministic native field/list order. Each distinct exact manifest opened is charged through the same invocation `LogicalWork.open`. Traversed ordinary fields charge `objectMemberRead`; items charge `listItemRead`; type edges charge `typeEdgeFollowed`. Deduplicate exact cycles within this definition traversal; do not regard a cycle visit as successful native certification. Then certify with goal `definition`. Do not evaluate a definition's declared minimum, maximum, enumeration or required-value constraints against the definition as if it were a value. Owning proofs use the native evidence verifier. Only successful native definition certification establishes this definition obligation.

For `value`, use an edition-specific traversal retaining the existing `LogicalWork.visit` scalar/list/object predicate accounting on the selected contextual Recipe, including its comparisons, text blocks, integer limbs, member examinations and pending value-proof keys. The old `carriedRoots` early return is disabled: a captured/portable source identity alone is not successful contextual value coverage. The old `previous` equality shortcut is likewise disabled unless the corresponding same-invocation contextual value obligation already succeeded. Do not call the old unmodified `visit` as the new reference algorithm. Its traversal is rooted at the selected Recipe, not the surrounding document. Then require both native strict selected evidence and `NativeRuntime.validate(selectedRecipe, context, "value")`. Publish the logical pending proof keys only after both checks succeed. A prior container or definition obligation does not enter that value-proof set. Do not pass an enclosing whole-root `previous` value to skip a changed contextual requirement; unchanged-subtree reuse requires the same contextual Recipe key and previously successful value coverage in this invocation.

In the new edition, establishing the identity of an explicit `Exact.Ref` reuses that reference's exact identifier. This identity-only case returns `local=false` and MUST NOT open the referenced body, rebuild it or charge identity hashing for that body, including when the reference appears as a part of local identity construction. It MUST NOT establish an `established` fact, a value certificate or successful contextual value coverage. Constructed local values retain their existing native identity construction and hash charges. A later required value read or owning-proof verification still establishes its own native obligations; an explicit reference is not evidence of its target's validity. This clarification does not alter legacy edition tariffs.

Handler ordering, BEX execution, patch construction/generalization, graph construction, emitted-event accounting and semantic exact identity construction retain their existing tariff operations. Replace only calls whose old purpose was whole-root validation with the declared obligation algorithm. Record preparation/serialization and fresh transport verification do not add independent semantic gas; exact identity construction already charged by the semantic operation is not charged again because an exporter chooses a different equivalent record encoding. No charge depends on whether a deferred child happens to be locally available.

Post-mutation checks observe enclosing containers afresh if their contextual Recipe changed, validate the changed value in its resulting context, and recheck native structural/lifetime invariants before finalization. A failed required read, predicate, record preparation or capability prerequisite leaves the input snapshot, prior prepared package, archive and completion registry unpublished. Snapshot wire identity and original event references are never rewritten to encode obligation state.

Qualification MUST compare full/missing and warm/cold logical results for these rules, including a single exact ID read in two different contextual Recipes, container-then-value aliasing, chunk continuation and failed-attempt retry. These are new-edition tariffs; old edition golden gas and receipts remain unchanged.

The next normal-path qualification is: restore a supported managed graph, execute the existing native counter/typed/workflow primitives, establish normal completion, capture and receive it, export, open a fresh processor and perform the next operation. Required-resource rollback and malformed/cyclic evidence are separate negative cases. This slice must use an actual generated candidate edition identity before it is selected by the public runtime; internal policy tests prior to that binding do not claim old-edition conformance.

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Demand-scoped Contracts — conformance proposal and release gates

Companion to [normative design draft](contracts-demand-scoped-draft.md). Status: required cases proposed for a new immutable edition; no claim that current Java/reference algorithms pass. Old final-gas cases remain unchanged. These cases must be represented in the canonical executable reference and Java tests before publication is qualified.

## Comparison rules

A is the preserved old build/edition/packages/journal. B is the candidate build with exactly those old inputs. Compare complete observations, BlueIds, snapshots, receipts, scalar gas, checkpoints, terminal decisions and subsequent cold operations exactly.

C uses the candidate build and the same new exact input sources/publications across variants. Compare full/missing-unused content, inline/reference, warm/cold, embedded/standalone and same-edition participants exactly. Do not compare differing publication IDs between A and C as though they were the same document. Do not normalize gas, checkpoints or internal observation fields to obtain equality.

Each failure test must distinguish missing resources from invalid content and unsupported semantics. Fixture/setup failures are not evidence for the intended assertion. Keep the original signed bytes, target flags and source order.

## Native obligations and evidence

| ID | Construction / action | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DS01 | Plain counter with original event Ref and unavailable unused historical operand | Normal new-edition process and export succeed; full/missing results and gas agree; ordinary full Language strict still requires that operand |
| DS02 | Exact native type discovery on an unused workflow whose step body is unavailable | Discover handler role/order without opening step body; selecting that handler later produces exact resource demand |
| DS03 | Conditional expression selects x; y body unavailable | x branch executes without fetching y; condition or contextual schema that actually requires y instead waits; no missing-to-false coercion |
| DS04 | Count constrained by parent `valueType`, typed field, inherited constraint and own schema | Standalone scalar certificate is insufficient; contextual valid value succeeds, invalid mutation fails, missing applicable definition waits |
| DS05 | `contracts` map schema `maxFields:0`; analogous list `itemType` and governing required fields | Invalid container rejected although every child would pass independently; constraints survive inline/reference representations |
| DS06 | Missing/invalid selected-node `specification`, type ancestry, labels, fixed values or merge metadata | Same native outcomes as complete contextual Language checks; no hand-written approximation or broad metadata omission |
| DS07 | Patch changes enclosing schema/type/valueType while child exact ID remains unchanged | Prior contextual success cannot be reused; new obligations fail/wait before exposing candidate to next step |
| DS08 | Same missing BlueId appears as unused historical target and current required operand | Historical identity observation succeeds; required role demands exact content; caches and delivery order do not alter result |
| DS09 | Ordinary event observer with selected metadata filter, nested filter and explicit private operand read | Native match/mismatch semantics preserved; required reads wait; ordinary observer not suppressed merely because operation routing skips |
| DS10 | Partial restore then full strict, warm repeated failure, cold restore, cache-pressure/reuse control | No partial fact is a full certificate; same logical decisions/gas and exact required IDs under all variants |

## Restore, atomicity and retention

| ID | Construction / action | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DS11 | Tampered envelope/commitment/release/runtime/member key/edge/lifetime/protected marker | Restore rejects for the actual corruption, with state/evidence/cache rollback |
| DS12 | Checkpoint subtype adds constraints; timestamp is an exact scalar reference | Apply actual contextual constraints; selected scalar projection validates integer; no identity or persisted-byte rewrite |
| DS13 | Excluded private operand inline inside a retained ancestor vs ordinary reference | Same exact IDs and results; exported records contain no excluded private body; shallow serialization does not drop required evidence |
| DS14 | Genuine cyclic member and owning-set proof; altered proof/body; historical A(T)→B(T)→A(T−1) | Correct proof/body survives cold restore; invalid proof fails; no acyclic exact record emitted for a cyclic identity; history remains historical |
| DS15 | First patch installed/finalized, then BEX read needs unavailable exact resource | NEEDS returns original state/checkpoint, previous context/evidence/prepared output/archive/provenance; first mutation demonstrably occurred, not only a failed candidate |
| DS16 | Same process receives only required record and retries exact input/event/time | One successful effect, complete strict/full reference equality within new edition; repeat committed event follows actual reference idempotency behavior |
| DS17 | Real required-retention failure, plus explicit fault injection after APPLIED calculation | No capturable completion, archive/progress/effects or evidence from failed attempt; distinguish natural missing-resource repro from injected transaction test |
| DS18 | Scoped export alone into empty process, then real next operation | No parent test runtime/evidence leaks; required content demand and constraints reconstructed from exact records; original event Ref retained |

## Completion and integration

| ID | Construction / action | Required observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DS19 | Successful local new-edition outcome, capture complete owned unit, normal receive and dependent reaction | Actual provenance established after required retention; received state/effects correct without pretending source closure is fully certified |
| DS20 | Foreign issuer, copied descriptor, modified receipt/event/time/release/runtime, expired capability, partial unit or wrong predecessor | Existing integrity checks reject; an exact after-body alone does not establish execution |
| DS21 | Atomically committed local record, fresh worker CompletionReader, receive then next operation | Trusted local origin plus descriptor/commitment checks re-established; arbitrary imported snapshot cannot manufacture provenance |
| DS22 | Crash before/after content fetch and before/after durable publication | One journal transaction owns completed state/evidence/progress/effects; pending demand survives; no lost wake or duplicate effect |
| DS23 | Actual authorized provider supplies required content after wait | Native continuation succeeds; unauthorized/missing provider response remains waiting or denied under existing host rules; manual addEvidence alone is not acceptance evidence |
| DS24 | Same process alternates old/new accounts with shared package caches | A/B old results remain exact; new policy never contaminates old bindings/certificates; incompatible cross-edition document processing is not silently enabled |
| DS25 | New-edition actual typed Order with Activation, existing timelines, exact Order mandate | Seller/Partner embedded and Customer standalone equal at all stable prefixes, both operations and restart; no unnecessary Agreement-version fetch; normal completion/journal, not overlay |

DS25 additionally requires Coordination's separately specified Q06/Q13 cases: exact/nonexact/no target, stale/future/foreign, incomplete own history, ordinary observer, child birth/prebirth/ties, initialized attach/rebase and historical cycles. Contracts-only PASS does not discharge those cases. Agent absent, Agreement-only, revoked and temporarily missing required proof are distinct cases; admission is not business execution.

## Experimental evidence and migration of assertions

The preserved run97407 demonstrates DS15/DS16 only for an isolated fixed two-step counter. It records assigned/finalized count2, NEEDS for the actual private record, rollback to count1, one-record retry and exact strict observations/gas708; repeat committed event gas160 matches strict reference. Run85630 adds repeated overflow/replay/capture refusal within that restricted overlay. Run51631 validates the plain profile after the shared compiler change. None establishes new-edition completion or signed Order integration.

Keep these artifacts and old tests unchanged as historical evidence. Port their assertions into normal edition-selected Java tests. The new normal completion tests expect established capture; historical overlay tests continue to expect `UNESTABLISHED_SOURCE_COMPLETION`. Do not reinterpret them as the same API guarantee.

## Publication gate

Before changing canonical package selection or generating a candidate publication:

1. Resolve D1–D5 in the design draft and inventory the actual native handler primitives.
2. Integrate the prose and obligation algorithms into a complete new specification with executable reference routines; reconcile every inherited full-certification/closure call explicitly.
3. Give restore/event/patch/finish/retain/export/cold/receive equivalent implementations and meaningful negative cases, not only YAML changes.
4. Build exact IDs using repository tooling, preserve old archives, then bind the candidate runtime to those generated identities.
5. Record which cases are PASS, FAIL, NOT_RUN or BLOCKED with exact source/publication IDs. Missing tests are not implicit passes.
6. Qualify A/B and C separately, including actual network/provider and journal restart; then enable the qualified new binding only for new registrations.

No external registry publication, account migration, push, merge or deployment is authorized by this proposal.
"}

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Language

Blue Language defines immutable typed content graphs, exact BlueIds, specialization, schemas, reusable packages, and references to additional protocol semantics.

## Read the specification

`SPECIFICATION.md` is the complete normative document for Blue Language 1.0, edition `blue-language/2026-09-26-specification-metadata-1`. It includes the core registry, ordinary Package and Protocol Specification definitions, and complete executable algorithms. No separate Blue specification is needed to determine this edition's Language rules.

`SPECIFICATION.html` in the source workspace is a generated reading view of the same Markdown. The Markdown is the identified normative Text. In the data-only `.bluepkg` artifact, read `spec/language.md`; it contains exactly the same document.

## Contents

- `types/` contains the six core registry bodies and the two ordinary standard definitions. Package and Protocol Specification are the package's two named exports; core names are established by the Language registry itself.
- `conformance/` contains unchanged portable Language cases and additional release checks.
- `dist/` contains the built package archive, exact package root, records, and manifest. Its `spec/language.md` is byte-identical to the source `SPECIFICATION.md`; `docs/types/` contains the same type sources. Archive conformance JSON arrays preserve the original case objects from the source JSONL files.
- `reference/python/` preserves the selected Python implementation and the support resources it imports. Those source copies are implementation evidence; older prose files retained inside that snapshot are not additional normative documents for this publication.
- `tools/` contains a local publisher and verifier. It performs no remote publication.
- `verification/` records the scope and results of the actual checks for this delivery.

## Local use

The commands below run from this source workspace, not from the unpacked data-only artifact. Python 3.13 or newer is required. The reference includes its YAML reader. Running the metadata regression tests also requires pytest.

```sh
./blue-package verify
./blue-package inspect
./blue-package test
python3.13 examples/use_package.py
```

A deliberate package build is:

```sh
./blue-package build
```

Normal verification and testing do not update pins, regenerate expected results, or change any referenced implementation source. Package acquisition is independent of Language interpretation; this project does not contact a registry.

## Identity and versioning

The package has a BlueId calculated under the selected Language. Archive and file checksums are separate integrity identifiers. This complete publication has a new package identity; it does not automatically replace the Language package referenced by existing BEX, Contracts, Coordination, or application packages.

Published definitions retain their exact IDs. The eight supplied registry/standard definitions and the executable Language algorithms are unchanged from the selected reference. Adoption by a dependent package is an explicit new dependency selection, not an identity rewrite.

This edition defines no automatic cross-Language import or cycle conversion. One selected interpretation governs an entire cyclic identity set and its proof. Compatible behavior, if introduced by a later Language edition, must be specified by that edition; no compatibility registry or version-range resolver is required here.

## Publication

The package can be retained locally or distributed through any file or artifact service. `dist/package.bluepkg` is the data artifact. GitHub and OCI are optional distribution infrastructure, not authorities that assign its BlueId. Nothing in this delivery has been published to an external registry.
"}

{"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue BEX

BEX evaluates explicit inputs into a value, ordered proposed changes and events,
and a deterministic admitted gas total. It does not apply document changes.

## Final gas edition

`1.0.0-final-gas.1` checks each charge before work and accumulates scalar gas.
Results have `value`, `changeset`, `events` and `gas_used`; accepted-charge rows
and `gas_trace` are not part of this edition. The default standalone allowance
remains 10,000,000. A supplied shared meter is never reset. Local and shared caps
retain their rejection order and one compact first-rejected-charge diagnostic.
A meter that has rejected work cannot resume accepting charges.

`SPECIFICATION.md` and `spec/bex-final-gas.md` contain the identical complete
normative text and six executable modules. The exact overrides and hashes are
listed in `docs/sources.json`. The earlier specification remains in `spec/bex.md`
and the frozen references remain unchanged for historical qualification.

This is a new exact protocol identity. Hosts must retain the old edition when
replaying old histories. Loading package data does not install an evaluator or
authorize an intrinsic. Optional debug traces are noncanonical and off by default.

## Local verification

With Python 3.13+, pytest, PyYAML, Java 21 and `BLUE_JAVA_CLASSPATH` pointing to
the qualified native Language runtime:

```sh
./blue-package verify
./blue-package test
python ../tools/build_final_gas.py blue-bex --check
```

The new-edition tests execute the finite conformance vectors and cover shared
meters, exact budgets, rejection and the absence of charge history. Historical
reference tests must run against their original frozen edition. Passing a finite
corpus does not establish universal conformance; see `QUALIFICATION.md`.
"}

H7WiYQ6GiWypRdFyWRcv99dsvTv6WnJYnu9eLYPQ.text: {"type":{"blueId":"GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC"},"value":"# Blue Language 1.0 ## Specification — 26 September 2026 **Edition:** `blue-language/2026-09-26-specification-metadata-1` **Publication:** complete specification, including standard definitions and normative algorithms ### Abstract Blue is a language for immutable, content-addressed graphs. Its nodes describe values, reusable definitions, constraints, and references to other nodes. A node may be used as a type: it contributes compatible structure and requirements without losing the identity of either the type or its instance. A BlueId identifies exact content, not a mutable name, a location, or a resolved interpretation. This specification defines the node model, portable input representations, exact identity, specialization, schemas, list construction, graph access, validation, specification metadata, and the standard package model. It also defines how a processor associates additional meaning with identified specifications. Particular workflow, coordination, rendering, query, and other application protocols define their own behavior; installing their content does not install an implementation. ### Status and authority This document is the complete normative definition of this edition. Its prose, tables, standard definitions, and normative algorithm annex form one contract. No separate Blue document, source-repository branch, release tag, implementation guide, or project discussion supplies an unstated rule. Examples marked informative illustrate the rules and do not extend them. A conformance claim identifies this edition and the implemented role. Publishing this document or a package containing it does not certify an implementation. A conflict between normative prose and algorithms is a specification defect; it is not permission to choose a convenient interpretation or regenerate expected results. ### Requirement terms **MUST** and **REQUIRED** state absolute requirements. **MUST NOT** and **PROHIBITED** state absolute prohibitions. **SHOULD** states a recommendation that may be departed from only after understanding and documenting the consequences. **SHOULD NOT** recommends against a practice under the same condition. **MAY** and **OPTIONAL** indicate permitted alternatives. Requirements expressed with these terms apply only to the role and operation being specified. ### Contents - [1. Scope, conformance roles, and interpretation](#scope) - [2. Nodes, graphs and operation roles](#model) - [3. Serialization, scalar codecs and empty content](#parsing) - [4. Exact normalization and BlueId](#identity) - [5. References, verified graph access and materialization](#graph) - [6. Types, specialization and validation goals](#types) - [7. Schemas: predicates, narrowing and conjunction](#schemas) - [8. Lists and specialization](#lists) - [9. Preprocessing and Source preparation](#preprocessing) - [10. Complete and selected resolution](#resolution) - [11. Validated creation, canonical authoring, minimization and export](#admission) - [12. Cyclic identities and owning-set proofs](#cycles) - [13. Diagnostics and safe operation boundaries](#diagnostics) - [14. Conformance and operation equivalence](#conformance) - [15. Worked examples — informative](#worked-examples) - [16. Authoring bindings and exact content availability](#authoring-bindings) - [17. Specification metadata](#specification-metadata) - [18. Standard packages and protocol descriptors](#packages) - [19. Edition selection and cyclic identity boundaries](#edition-boundaries) - [20. Protocol interpretation and document processors](#processors) - [Appendix A. Algorithm notation and primitive operations](#notation) - [Appendix B. Exact registry and preprocessing selectors](#registry) - [Appendix C. Ordinary standard definitions](#standard-definitions) - [Appendix D. Complete normative algorithms](#algorithms) - [Appendix E. Portable conformance-request protocol](#fixture-protocol) - [Appendix F. Exact repository carrier](#repository-carrier) ## 1. Scope, conformance roles, and interpretation ### 1.1 Content model Blue represents information as a graph of immutable typed nodes. A document is one root together with the portion of the graph presently materialized. Types are themselves nodes. Using a node as a type contributes requirements, fixed content, and compatible structure to the instance. Language operations establish exact content, its identity, or specific conclusions about its meaning. They do not grant authority or perform external business actions. This edition defines no workflow scheduler, transaction coordinator, network service, database layout, or portable execution gas tariff. **LANG-SCOPE.** An implementation MUST apply the structural Language rules to all reserved fields, including `contracts`, without inferring execution behavior from the field name. Application protocols MUST NOT change the Language rules used to parse, identify, or resolve content in an established interpretation context. ### 1.2 Conformance roles A **Language implementation** provides the content and operation semantics defined in this document. A **package processor** additionally constructs, verifies, or mounts packages according to §18. A **protocol processor** performs a stated task under additional identified protocol rules, according to §20. A single program may perform several roles; a reader may perform only the Language role. **LANG-AUTHORITY.** Full Language conformance requires the operation contracts in this document, not only structural hashing. An implementation MAY organize its APIs, records, storage, caches, and algorithms differently, provided that it preserves the required observations, identities, proof obligations, and failure distinctions. A subset implementation MUST identify its supported subset and MUST NOT advertise omitted behavior as supported. The executable notation in Appendix D specifies complete Blue-specific procedures. Python allocation, private attributes, diagnostic English, and reference cache layout are not required interfaces. The selected mathematical and serialization behavior is required. The six core registry bodies in Appendix B are exact content; they are not illustrative substitutes. ### 1.3 Selecting Language An **interpretation context** fixes the Language edition, core registry, input role, explicitly selected authoring bindings, and the evidence and resource controls available to an operation. The Language selection is established before processing identity-bearing content. An ordinary `type` reference or a document's `specification` metadata does not retroactively choose a different parser, identity algorithm, or registry. **LANG-VERSION.** All steps of one identity, resolution, or admission calculation MUST use one coherent selection of Language rules. A content address MUST NOT be reassigned to different exact content. Retained content and validation evidence MUST NOT be silently reinterpreted under a different edition. Compatibility and cyclic identity boundaries are specified in §19. A bootstrap Language package identifies its selected rules and standard definitions; it is verified by an implementation already able to interpret those rules. It does not install or derive that implementation. Its own identifier is not embedded into the content from which that same identifier is calculated. ### 1.4 Exact identity, availability, and trust An identifier and a body are different kinds of evidence. A correct identifier identifies content. It neither makes the content available nor establishes its author's authority. A correctly identified body is not necessarily a valid completed value or a supported protocol. Admission and support assertions MUST distinguish these claims. Registry addresses, source paths, release labels, timestamps, and display aliases are not alternative BlueIds. An established provider result is interpreted only in the role and context under which its content can be verified. --- ## 2. Nodes, graphs and operation roles ### Purpose Separate **what a node contains**, **how it is represented**, and **what an operation proves**. These distinctions determine whether two inputs should have the same identity and whether successful hashing is enough to admit a document. ### 2.1 Exact content and an effective view An exact node has its own fields, literal metadata, scalar payload or list elements. Its effective view additionally applies the inherited declarations and compatible constraints relevant to that node. Resolution retains the exact origin; it does not overwrite that origin with its view. **LANG-EXACT-VIEW.** Two distinct exact nodes MAY resolve to identical effective views. An implementation MUST NOT infer identity equality from that observation alone, or recover a lost exact origin by guessing from a bare resolved view. The ordinary hasher identifies exact content, not a resolver object. For example, Text PLN and Currency PLN retain different own type edges. An enclosing Holder declaration may interpret either as Currency PLN. Their exact child identities remain different. All five complete instance inputs appear in §15. ### 2.2 A reference is not an overlay A pure reference has exactly one member: ```yaml blueId: GX7CFUmSDrE2MzptunLCCdZwnuwwrenRQqEnHL4x3uoC ``` The same object with a sibling, even a null sibling, is invalid. To specialize a referenced node, place the reference under `type` and supply instance fields outside it. Expansion reveals an existing node; specialization creates a new, more constrained node. **LANG-REFERENCE.** A reference and its verified exact materialization denote the same node. At a complete node-valued position, replacing one with the other MUST preserve exact identity. A semantic operation MUST NOT expose the reference wrapper as an ordinary `blueId` field. Its conclusions depend on the selected operation and verified content, not expansion state. A reference to a compiled list result is exact content. It is not a reusable Source instruction that should be executed at its new location. Representation equivalence applies to a node and its exact representation, not to an unevaluated constructor expression and an unrelated exact operand. ### 2.3 The node model A materialized node contains reserved metadata and at most one primary payload. Scalars use `value`; lists use `items`; objects use direct ordinary child fields. A metadata-only node may have no payload. The empty map `{}` is a present empty object, not a missing declaration. Bare objects do not acquire a Dictionary type, and bare lists do not acquire a List type, merely through normalization. **LANG-NODE-SHAPE.** A node MUST NOT combine scalar, list and ordinary-object payloads. The reserved-invalid fields `properties` and `constraints` MUST be rejected. Ordinary keys colliding with reserved fields cannot be represented directly as application map keys; an application-defined escaped structure is required. | Field | Role and permitted shape | Identity contribution | |---|---|---| | `name`, `description` | Literal Unicode string | Literal string | | `specification` | Complete reference-valued metadata; explicit node in Source, exact reference after preparation; see §17 | Exact target identity | | `type`, `itemType`, `keyType`, `valueType` | Complete node; Source alias before preprocessing; exact reference afterward | Exact defining-node identity | | `value` | Scalar literal, never an object or sequence | Own-type encoded literal | | `items` | Sequence slot, not a separately replaceable node slot | Ordered payload-list identity | | `blueId` | Final identifier, exclusively in a pure reference | The identifier itself | | `blue` | Source-root preprocessing configuration only | Absent from the resulting content | | `schema` | Exact node interpreted using §7 | Exact child identity | | `mergePolicy` | Literal `positional` or `append-only` | Identity of the corresponding core Text scalar | | `contracts` | Exact node interpreted as a content map when needed | Exact child identity | | Any ordinary field | One complete child node | Exact child identity | For example, `name: {blueId: ...}` is invalid: a label is literal metadata, not a node slot. To reference a list, replace the whole list node, not the `items` sequence slot. ### 2.4 Input roles | Role | Meaning | May execute Source construction? | |---|---|---| | **Source** | Authored document with optional directive, aliases and construction expressions | Yes, once | | **Preprocessed Source** | Baseline-normalized Source; controls can remain | Yes, at compilation | | **Exact** | Already-established complete content, possibly partially materialized | No | | **Direct** | Exact input with every type and specification position already a pure reference | No | | **Compact canonical wire** | Explicit codec using verified list-prefix records | Decode, never replay Source | | **Effective result** | Interpretation bound to exact origins and coverage | Not an exact-input replacement | **LANG-INPUT-ROLE.** Every operation MUST establish the role of its input before interpreting it. JSON versus YAML does not select the role. Loading a published exact body MUST NOT execute its contents as new Source. A failed verification MUST NOT be retried under other modes until an identity happens to match. ### 2.5 Abstract operations The names below identify contracts, not mandatory SDK method names. `Context` means the fixed Language/registry/bindings, any explicitly selected out-of-band resource controls and available verified or verifiable evidence. Returning an identity alone never establishes semantic validity. | Operation | Input role | Output | Evidence | Guarantee | |---|---|---|---|---| | EXACT_ID | prepared exact Node/Ref | exact identity | identities of complete child contributions; bodies only for preparation that requires them | none | | PREPARE_SOURCE | Source and fixed environment | constructed exact node + new dependencies | preprocessing and actual construction dependencies | structural preparation; not whole admission | | ADMIT_SOURCE | Source + explicit definition/value goal | validated canonical exact result + artifacts | complete required graph/type evidence | whole-graph admission; root duplicate normalization | | ADMIT_EXACT | existing exact input + goal | validated same exact node + artifacts | complete required graph/type evidence | whole-graph admission; no migration | | ADMIT_DIRECT | strict Direct input + goal | validated same exact node + artifacts | complete required graph/type evidence | Direct type-slot grammar plus admission | | ADMIT_CANONICAL | compact wire + goal | decoded validated exact node + artifacts | prefix, type and required graph evidence | admission after the declared codec | | RESOLVE_COMPLETE / CERTIFY | prepared exact input/recipe + goal | effective head and certified obligations | requested definition/active value closure | specified semantic closure | | OBSERVE | exact input, path and question | established / absent / incomplete / invalid | dependency closure of this question | only declared coverage | | LOOKUP_EXACT | exact graph and pointer | exact child, literal, sequence or absence | required direct navigation evidence | no contextual Source reconstruction | | SPLIT_FRAGMENTS | exact graph and complete-node cuts | same root plus exact fragment map | selected nodes and structural ancestors | identity-preserving materialization | | REFINE_EXACT | ordered exact base and overlay | complete exact compatible result | required exact operands and declarations | preserves inherited guarantees; not arbitrary edit | | CHECK_SUBTYPE | candidate and parent definitions | Boolean or invalid/incomplete result | needed type and preservation evidence | specified subtype relation | | REFINE_SCHEMA | ordered inherited/authored schemas | constraints or refined exact schema | schema operands and required domains | no explicit weakening | | CONJOIN_SCHEMA | independent constraint descriptors | combined internal constraints | previously established predicates | conjunction, not override admission | | EXPAND / COLLAPSE | exact graph + complete-node paths | another materialization | navigation and selected exact nodes | same exact identities | | MINIMIZE | certified exact origin + goal | valid Source and available dependencies | enough evidence for the round trip | same required effective view; ID may change | | ENCODE_EXACT / DECODE_EXACT | exact content / exact wire | identity-preserving exact representation | declared dependencies | codec, not Source compilation | | ENCODE_COMPACT / DECODE_COMPACT | exact content / compact wire | identity-preserving compact representation | selected prefix evidence | codec, not Source replay | | FINALIZE_SET / VERIFY_MEMBER | symbolic set / owning-set proof | master/mapping or verified member | complete set boundary and proof | exact set addressing; admission separate | **LANG-ADMISSION-CLAIM.** Structural naming MUST NOT be presented as semantic admission. An operation claiming whole-document admission MUST establish the required exact graph and type definitions, then certify its explicit goal. A selected observation MUST NOT be used as whole-document certification. Definition and completed-value goals are distinct proof obligations, not different Blue node kinds. ### 2.6 Fundamental relationships | Relationship | Required distinction | |---|---| | Exact equality | Includes own labels, type and all identity-bearing content | | Scalar predicate comparison | Uses effective domain and the specified payload rules | | Preservation | May permit additional object fields while retaining inherited guarantees | | Subtype | Uses the specified structural/nominal relation, not a matching name | | Semantic round trip | Preserves the observations defined by `same_view`; need not preserve Source ID | | Availability | Missing evidence is neither an absent field nor a valid target | **Algorithm:** A01 defines records and invariants; A03 defines exact identity; A06 defines effective recipes. `OPERATIONS` in the annex composes existing algorithms into the abstract operation contracts without a storage or receipt dependency. --- ## 3. Serialization, scalar codecs and empty content ### Purpose and input Parse one JSON or portable YAML document into the shared node model without losing distinctions that determine identity. Formatting outside strings is not content. Parsed strings and number categories are content-bearing inputs to the subsequent codec. ### 3.1 Text parsing **LANG-PARSE.** Read exactly one document. Reject duplicate decoded keys, non-string map keys, malformed Unicode and invalid syntax. A document root MUST NOT be null. JSON `\u` escapes use ASCII hexadecimal digits; valid surrogate pairs decode to one Unicode scalar, and unpaired surrogates fail. A parser MUST NOT replace malformed input with replacement characters. Numeric tokens retain this complete ASCII grammar until scalar encoding: ```text -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)? ``` A token with neither point nor exponent is integer-spelled. A token with either is decimal/exponent-spelled. Thus bare `1` and `1.0` are not interchangeable inference inputs. **LANG-YAML.** YAML supplies presentation syntax only. Quoted and block scalars are strings. An empty plain scalar or exactly `null` is null; exactly `true` and `false` are Boolean; a full JSON-number match is a retained number token; other permitted plain text is a string. Reject anchors, aliases, explicit tags, directives, merge-key syntax, multiple documents and non-JSON data types. Quoted `"<<"` is an ordinary string key. Plain `True`, `~`, `01`, `.inf` and date-looking text are not implicit Boolean, null, numeric or timestamp values. **LANG-TEXT.** Preserve parsed strings exactly. Do not trim, case-fold, normalize Unicode, normalize line endings inside parsed strings, or remove block-scalar trailing newlines. YAML folding and chomping determine the parsed string. Different resulting strings may identify different nodes even when they look similar. ### 3.2 Wrappers and nulls A bare scalar and a `value`-only wrapper normalize alike. A bare list and an `items`-only wrapper normalize alike. Explicit additional metadata remains content. **LANG-EMPTY.** In ordinary objects, remove null-valued members but preserve an object left empty. Never remove a list position. Source list null becomes the designated hole. Exact and Direct list null is invalid. `{}`, `[]`, absence, empty Text and the hole are distinct. | Input | Exact-normalization consequence | |---|---| | `{x: null}` | `{}` | | `{x: {y: null}}` | `{x: {}}`; the `x` edge remains | | `{value: null}` | `{}` | | `{blueId: X, extra: null}` | Invalid mixed reference, before null removal | | Source `[null, {}, []]` | `[HOLE, {}, []]`, three positions | | `[1,2]` and `{items:[1,2]}` | Same payload-only list | | `{type: List, items:[1,2]}` | Different exact node with an explicit type edge | The hole is the ordinary exact object `{$empty:true}`. Its exact identity is `6V647wzsPU3zXvrc5AwKsqbFmkgHWV8WAeyBfNG1T8Rx`. A reference to that node has the same hole behavior. `{$empty:false}` or the same object with additional metadata is ordinary different content. Hole-filling permission applies only at the list-specialization positions specified in §8. ### 3.3 Own-type scalar encoding **LANG-SCALAR-INFERENCE.** Without an own type, strings infer Text, Booleans infer Boolean, safe integer-spelled numbers infer Integer, and decimal/exponent numbers infer Double. No automatic container type is inferred. Converting an untyped decimal token to an integer because its current value is integral is not permitted. The safe unquoted Integer interval is `[-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]`, inclusive. | Exact own type | Admitted input and exact output | |---|---| | **Integer** | Decode an integral numeric token exactly, or a canonical decimal Integer string. Store safe results as numbers and larger results as quoted canonical decimal strings. | | **Double** | Decode an admitted decimal token/string to the nearest finite binary64 value, ties to even. Both zero signs have one commitment. | | **Text** | Require a string. No automatic stringification. | | **Boolean** | Require a Boolean. No truthiness or string-to-Boolean conversion. | | **Custom type** | Retain the exact own type ID. Strings and Booleans stay their literal category; safe integral numeric spellings share the canonical numeric payload; other finite numeric values use binary64. Do not fetch ancestry merely to choose an intrinsic identity codec. | **LANG-INTEGER-CODEC.** An unsafe integer-spelled token fails; quoted canonical decimal with explicit Integer is the portable representation. An explicit-Integer decimal/exponent token is evaluated as an exact decimal rational and must be integral. Canonical Integer strings forbid `+`, whitespace, leading zeros, `-0`, fractions and exponents. Numeric zero spellings normalize to zero. A natively tagged mathematical Integer is not a parsed unsafe number token. **LANG-DOUBLE-CODEC.** Binary64 parsing uses round-to-nearest, ties-to-even. Nonfinite results fail; finite underflow to zero is permitted. Do not use an implementation-specific epsilon or decimal rounding during later comparisons. Integer-looking helper output does not change a Double node's type. Formatting follows the exact algorithm in A03, not a host's default floating-point display. **LANG-CUSTOM-CODEC.** Intrinsic own-type encoding and contextual interpretation are separate. Resolution may interpret canonical Text under an inherited Integer requirement without rewriting that exact Text node.
